justification: The route map on the evidence page now sits on a real street map: the NSW Spatial Services Base Map tiles (roads with names, lot lines, house numbers, parks, stations), drawn as images under our routes in the same SVG. The routes and the tiles use the same Web Mercator projection so a line cannot drift off its street. A tile that fails to load is not drawn, so the plain background and the busy-road dots remain; when a tile has loaded the dots are hidden and the basemap is credited under the map. No new dependency, no data change, no server change except one sentence in a note string. The tile source is one object (BASEMAP) so it can be swapped.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/route-map-geometry.test.ts __tests__/components/evidence-statement-page.test.tsx ; npx tsc --noEmit -p . ; python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_route_map.py -q -o addopts=
falsifiable_check.expected: Jest 60 passed; tsc 0 errors; Python 43 passed.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A tile is requested with row and column swapped, drawn over the routes, kept after it failed, credited before it loaded, placed from the wrong corner or at the wrong zoom; the routes use a different projection from the tiles; the dots stay after the map loads; or the scale bar is not in ground metres.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Eleven hand breakages each turned a test red and were restored: tile row and column swapped, tiles never drawn, a failed tile staying drawn, the basemap credited before any tile loaded, dots kept after the map loads (first missed, then a test on the dots themselves was added and it went red), north not up, padding in ground metres, one zoom too high, scale bar in Mercator metres, tiles placed from the wrong corner. Real render: headless Chrome with live tiles for 28 Selwyn Street (Pymble) and 60 Palace Street (Petersham): the routes follow the real streets and the road names, lot lines and station are readable. Typed-figure check 0 unlisted; wording check none.

pre_impl.existing_data: The route map was an inline SVG with a plain background and orange busy-road dots (PR 1671). The repo already loads NSW SIX tiles for aerial imagery (AerialTile.tsx) through maplibre; this does not use maplibre.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The reader found the NSW Base Map has street names, lot lines and house numbers but NO building footprints. OpenStreetMap's own tile server and the MapTiler/Stadia free tiers are not for commercial use, so building outlines are not included. The licence version (CC BY 3.0 or 4.0) and NSW's web-service terms are unconfirmed; the caption says 'Creative Commons Attribution'.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: Web Mercator projection, tile placement, a BASEMAP setting, tile images and a fallback. Unchanged: every route, distance, answer and data file.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A tile request that fails (service down, blocked, slow) is simply not drawn; the page shows today's plain map. No error is raised and no route is affected.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No data shape changes: the route map data from the server is the same.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A planner sees the walk on a street map with names. If tiles cannot load, they see the same plain map as before.

functions.name: mercator
functions.output: Web Mercator x and y in metres
functions.if_none: Latitudes beyond the Mercator limit are clamped, so the result is always finite.

functions.name: zoomFor
functions.input: the picture's side in Mercator metres, its pixel size and the service's top zoom
functions.output: the whole zoom level at which a tile is drawn at its own size or up to twice as large
functions.if_none: A zero, huge or non-numeric span gives a clamped finite zoom.

functions.name: tileUrl
functions.input: a zoom, tile column, tile row and an optional url template
functions.output: the tile address with z, y and x filled in the order this service uses
functions.if_none: The template comes from the BASEMAP setting.

functions.name: projectRouteMap
functions.input: a route map with latitude and longitude lines
functions.output: picture coordinates for the lines, busy dots, lot, end, a ground-metre scale bar, the zoom and the tiles under the picture
functions.if_none: No line with two points gives null.

functions.name: RouteMapFigure
functions.input: a route map from the evidence data
functions.output: the picture with street-map tiles under the routes, a legend and the basemap credit once a tile has loaded
functions.if_none: A failed tile is not drawn; with none loaded the plain map and the dots remain.

values.value: BASEMAP url template, zoom limit and attribution
values.if_missing: Not applicable: it is a constant in the file.

break_it.scenario: The NSW tile service is down, slow or blocked.
break_it.what_happens: Each failed tile is dropped; the plain background, the dots and the routes remain and the basemap is not credited.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: a tile is hidden on error and credited only after one has loaded.
break_it.how: The fallback Jest test fires an error on every tile.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/components/evidence-statement-page.test.tsx -t falls back

break_it.scenario: The routes are drawn in a different projection from the tiles.
break_it.what_happens: A line would sit off its street by up to tens of metres.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: one Mercator function places both, and tests check the start point lies in the tile that holds that latitude and longitude.
break_it.how: test 'the route stays on the tiles'.

break_it.scenario: A lot near the edge of a zoom level or a very long route.
break_it.what_happens: The zoom is clamped between 12 and the service limit and at most 25 tiles are requested.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: zoomFor clamps and a test checks the tile count and coverage.
break_it.how: test 'tiles cover the whole picture with no gap'.

break_it.scenario: The street map shows roads, so the orange dots would be clutter.
break_it.what_happens: The dots and their legend text are hidden once a tile has loaded.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: the dots follow the loaded state.
break_it.how: The tile Jest test checks no dot remains and the legend does not mention them.

residual_risk: 1) NSW web-service terms were not retrievable and the licence version (CC BY 3.0 or 4.0) is unconfirmed; ask NSW Spatial Services (customer hub) for written confirmation of terms and attribution wording. 2) The NSW Base Map has no building footprints; adding them needs a self-hosted OpenStreetMap map file (ODbL) or a paid provider, as OpenStreetMap's own tile server is not for commercial use. 3) Tiles are drawn at 1x to 2x their own size, so they can look soft on a large screen. 4) Our own labels for crossing types and unmarked crossings are not on the map yet.
